findings: Theorem 1 averages conditional continuity equations into the marginal equation only when differentiation/integration exchanges satisfy Leibniz regularity; the plan carries this as a proof condition.

Theorem 2 gives equality of conditional and marginal flow-matching objectives up to a parameter-independent constant, hence identical gradients, under positive p_t, bounded u_t/v_t/parameter derivatives, decay, Fubini and differentiability; these are now stated in the scope.

The Gaussian conditional field is derived from an invertible affine flow with sigma_t>0. The special conditional OT map is proved locally by a direct coupling/Cauchy–Schwarz bound; the source explicitly warns that conditional OT does not make the induced marginal flow OT. Training and sampling comparisons are empirical.

findings: Radford et al. define a batch of N matched pairs, normalize each encoder output, multiply pairwise dot products by exp(t)>0, and average the image-to-text and text-to-image cross-entropies on the diagonal targets; the scaffold now states positive logit scale s=e^tau.

The paper’s 400-million-pair WIT training, zero-shot prompt classifier/template averaging and transfer/robustness results are empirical choices/results, not a theorem from contrastive loss to universal transfer.

Main-text duplicate analysis is on PDF p. 8: 35 datasets, median overlap 2.2%, mean 3.2%, and little measured impact; no appendix claim is used. CLIP sampling/caption/task assumptions do not satisfy ML-51’s latent-class theorem contract by default.

findings: Bommasani et al. define a foundation model conceptually as broad-data (generally self-supervised, large-scale) pretraining followed by adaptation to many downstream tasks; the selected report sections cover modalities/ecosystem, training/adaptation and explicitly limited theory, not a theorem.

Kaplan et al. fit decoder-only Transformer cross-entropy scaling laws on WebText2: alpha_N≈0.076, alpha_D≈0.095 and compute-efficient alpha_Cmin≈0.050, with fitted compute allocation N∝Cmin^0.73, B∝Cmin^0.24, S∝Cmin^0.03. These are empirical frontier fits tied to tested model/data/compute ranges and tokenization; the caveats state no solid theoretical understanding and uncertain extrapolation.

The pretraining-adaptation interface remains an open theory problem in the report; prompt/in-context learning is not covered by a simple parameter-updating ERM adaptation framework. No universal emergence, modality-general transfer, OOD reliability or compute optimality theorem is claimed.

findings: Guo et al. define top-label calibration and binned ECE/MCE; ECE depends on the selected bins and is not a proper scoring rule. Positive-temperature softmax preserves argmax, and their scalar temperature is fitted by validation NLL; these empirical iid results do not imply shifted calibration.

Ovadia et al. is a 2019 empirical benchmark over specific data/modalities/shifts/methods. It separates shifted inputs with labels among known classes from fully OOD inputs whose true labels lie outside the label set; conclusions are restricted to those protocols, with no universal ensemble ranking.

MSF-37 supplies exact split-conformal order statistic k=ceil((m+1)(1-alpha)), +infinity sentinel when k=m+1, and marginal exchangeable coverage conditional on training; its shared-uniform randomized-rank set has exact marginal coverage. It supplies no covariate-conditional or shift guarantee.

source_evidence.citation: On Calibration of Modern Neural Networks — Chuan Guo, Geoff Pleiss, Yu Sun, Kilian Q. Weinberger (2017 (ICML / PMLR 70))
source_evidence.read_status: Main paper PDF pp. 1–8 read, including definition, method, evaluation, caveats and discussion. References/extra material pp. 9–10 were not read.

source_evidence.pair_audited_ranges: §2 top-label calibration, ECE/MCE and bin definitions, PDF pp. 2–3; §3 temperature scaling, p. 4; experiments/results and limitations, pp. 4–8. References pp. 9–10 not read or used.
source_evidence.source_claims: Defines top-label calibration and binned ECE/MCE; explains ECE is a bin-dependent approximation with resolution/estimation concerns, not a proper scoring rule. Scalar temperature on logits preserves argmax and is fitted by validation NLL. Reported calibration improvements are empirical on the tested in-distribution tasks.
source_evidence.hypotheses_and_proof_scope: Argmax invariance follows from preserving order for T>0. Validation fitting requires labeled data representative of the evaluation distribution for intended empirical calibration; no distribution-free finite-sample or shifted-distribution guarantee.
source_evidence.source_limits: Iid temperature scaling does not guarantee calibration under distribution shift. Binned calibration metrics depend on binning and sample size.

source_evidence.source_claims: Benchmark evaluates NLL, Brier, ECE, entropy/confidence, ensembles, and other uncertainty methods across specific image/text/tabular tasks and corruption/shift regimes.
